_comment: Settings > Fonts: the faces, sizes and magnification of the ChiSurf window, bound to FontSettingsModel (fonts_model.py). Every change applies on the next frame and is saved to gui.fonts. The 'font_preview' custom sections draw a sample line in a role's font (fonts_app.py): drawing in a chosen face is what a spec cannot express.
title: Fonts

sections.title: Interface
sections.description: The text of buttons, labels, menus, tables and tooltips, and the magnification of the whole window.

sections.label: Face
sections.description: Face of the interface text. monospace is the built-in face: the sharpest and fastest. Any installed family works; a proportional one lays out from its measured widths.

sections.label: Size
sections.description: Size of all interface text. Headings, captions and code follow it unless they have a size of their own. 8 pt is the shipped size.

sections.label: Magnification
sections.description: Magnifies the whole window -- text, spacing, icons and plots together, as a browser zoom does. 1.00 is actual size; 1.25 suits a high-resolution screen viewed from a distance.
A sample line in the interface face and size.

sections.title: Editor and console
sections.description: The Console dock, the code editor and code blocks in the documentation.

sections.label: Face
sections.description: Face of code. Only monospaced families are listed: the editor lines its columns up on a fixed character width. The code editor's own font setting, when changed there, takes precedence in that tool.

sections.label: Size
sections.description: Size of code in points. Same as interface (0) follows the interface size.
A sample line of code in the editor face and size.

sections.title: Documentation
sections.description: Running text, headings and captions of the Documentation dock and the help windows.

sections.label: Text face
sections.description: Face of running text and captions. prose picks Verdana, else DejaVu Sans: the proportional relatives of the built-in interface face.

sections.label: Text size
sections.description: Size of running text. Headings and captions are set relative to it. Same as interface (0) follows the interface size. The A− / A+ buttons of the Documentation dock zoom on top of it.

sections.label: Heading face
sections.description: Face of headings.

sections.label: Heading scale
sections.description: Ratio between neighbouring heading levels: a fourth-level heading is the text size times this, a page title times its fourth power. 1.125 is the shipped scale; 1.0 sets headings at the text size.

sections.label: Bold headings
sections.description: Set headings in the bold weight of their face.

sections.label: Caption size
sections.description: Size of figure captions and footnotes. One step below text (0) sets them one step of the heading scale below the text size.
A sample second-level heading.
A sample line of running text.
A sample caption.

sections.title: Formulas
sections.description: Mathematics in the documentation and in model descriptions.

sections.label: Face
sections.description: Text face of formulas; it needs an italic style. auto picks the first installed of STIX Two, Times New Roman and DejaVu Serif. Symbols the face lacks come from the installed mathematical faces.

sections.label: Size
sections.description: Size of formulas. Same as text (0) follows the documentation text size.
A sample formula.

sections.title: Rendering
sections.description: How the glyphs of installed faces are put on screen. The built-in interface face is a fixed bitmap and is not affected.

sections.label: Resolution
sections.description: Glyph raster scale. 1× draws one glyph pixel per screen pixel, placed on the pixel grid: the sharpest text. Higher values rasterise finer and scale down: smoother curves, slightly softer stems, more memory.

sections.label: Smooth edges
sections.description: Grey-scale anti-aliasing of glyph edges. Off draws hard black-and-white edges, which some people read more easily at small sizes. Hinting cannot be chosen: the rasteriser does not offer it.

sections.label: Fallback faces
sections.placeholder: e.g. Noto Sans CJK JP, Noto Sans Math
sections.description: Comma-separated faces tried, in order, for a character the chosen face does not have (CJK, mathematical symbols, subscripts), before the faces the system provides. A face may also be given a chain of its own: Inter, Verdana, prose.

buttons.label: Reset to defaults
buttons.description: Every font setting back to the shipped look, applied at once and saved.

sections.description: What the last change did.
